title: Stale-policy roll-forward during staggered rollout allows transient quota over-accepts for route-alias customers
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Multiple customer reports and internal telemetry show short windows (tens of seconds) where requests are accepted but the corresponding meter debit is not recorded, allowing orgs to exceed their configured quotas without being throttled. The issue is only observed during staggered/staged rollouts when route aliasing + per-route overrides are in use. Impact: affected customers see bursty unmetered periods (billing undercount and potential SLA exposure).
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy runtime change with two-phase rollout across edge shards (canary -> gradual). 2) Configure an org with a per-route quota and a route alias that maps to multiple underlying routes. 3) Send sustained small requests from a client that exercise route alias resolution across shards while the rollout is in progress. 4) Observe accepted responses while debit counters on the primary meter remain unchanged for ~10-45s, then reconcile with a sudden backlog of debits that effectively compensates but after the over-allow window has passed.
investigation_summary: Initial triage: telemetry shows a class of 'allow-without-debit' traces originating at edge nodes that had the older policy evaluator while shard leases were being transferred. Root cause hypothesis: a race between the deferred ack batching mechanism and a new fast-path evaluation added in runtime-1.20. During the staggered rollout, old-edge nodes continued to accept requests and batched usage ack messages to the central shard. When the new evaluator took over, it applied an optimistic fast-path acceptance if no current ledger entry existed for a (org,route_alias) key. Because the deferred ack batch had been queued but not yet applied, the fast-path allowed more requests. When the queued batch was processed later, credits were applied retrospectively causing billing spikes but not preventing the earlier over-accept. Additional contributor: alias-to-route normalization was non-deterministic across evaluator versions, causing lookups to hit different internal keys (alias vs canonical route) between old and new nodes.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Pause staggered rollout and abort further canary expansion until fix is deployed. 2) Flip runtime feature-flag to disable the new fast-path acceptance heuristic in runtime-1.20 builds. 3) For affected customers, enable stricter consistency mode for quota checks (forces synchronous debit-path) via console switch. 4) Add alerting rule to detect 'allow_without_debit' pattern and notify on-call.
root_cause_and_fix: Root cause: race between deferred ack batching + non-idempotent ack application + a new fast-path acceptance optimization and inconsistent alias normalization across versions. Fixes planned: (A) make ack application idempotent with explicit op IDs and tombstone checks so late batches cannot cause an earlier acceptance window; (B) remove the fast-path acceptance when there is any pending shard handoff or when alias normalization version mismatch is detected; (C) unify alias normalization and include the canonical route key in ledger keys so both versions target the same key. Implementations will include unit tests and cross-version integration tests in the canary harness.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR with idempotent ack processing and alias canonicalization. 2) Deploy to internal canary with feature-flag off for fast-path. 3) Run synthetic workload for 30m to validate no 'allow_without_debit' traces. 4) Gradually enable fast-path only after adding a strong shard-handoff check and re-run tests. 5) Full rollout to prod after 48h monitoring with no regressions. Emergency rollback steps documented in the PR description.
test_plan: - Unit tests for ack idempotency and op-id collisions. - Integration test: dual-version evaluator harness that simulates staggered rollout and asserts no acceptance without debit. - Fuzz tests around alias normalization and ledger key generation. - Load test that exercises batching timeouts and confirms no undercount during lease transfers.
